How to Submit Public Comment:
Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of the following
methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit it to the City
Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes per person per item. At the
Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to allow all speakers to address the City Council.

Electronic submission of Public Comment is also available via the City’s website as noted below.
Public Comment submitted electronically will be read into the record. Words that would disrupt the
meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and discriminatory language, will not be read. Your
comments must be received by 5:00 P.M. on meeting day.

Website: Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at Public Comment.

   MINUTES OF WEDNESDAY, SEPTEMBER 13, 2023
  MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL
  LAS ADVISORY COMMITTEE SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA

CALL TO ORDER

Chair Lubisich called the special meeting of the LAS Advisory Committee to order at 5:03 p.m.
on Wednesday, September 13, 2023, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission
Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Commissioner Brenhaug.

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present:  Michelle Brenhaug, Beatriz Mojarro, Chasity Jennings-Nuñez, and
  Senya Lubisich

Commissioners Absent:  None

ANNOUNCMENTS
Manager Morales-Stevens provided information for the public on how to submit comments, and
how to request meeting agendas. If you wish to address the LAS Advisory Committee, e-mail all
public comments to HEARCommission@sgch.org.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  A motion was made by Vice Chair Jennings-Nuñez and seconded by
  Commissioner Mojarro to remove item 4A from agenda.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 4-0-0 as follows:
  Ayes: Brenhaug, Jennings-Nuñez, Lubisich, Mojarro
  Nays: None
  Abstain: None

LAS ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES  SEPTEMBER 13, 2023
   2. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Christina Salazar, a member of Tongva wants to make sure the committee honors and
  respects the tribe.

  3. ACTION ITEMS
  A motion was made by Commissioner Mojarro and seconded by Commissioner
  Brenhaug to approve the minutes for February 16, 2023.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 4-0-0 as follows:
  Ayes: Brenhaug, Jennings-Nuñez, Lubisich, Mojarro
  Nays: None
  Abstain: None

  4. DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A. REVIEW OF APPROVED ACTION PLAN

  This item was removed.

  B. FINALIZE LAND ACKNOWLEDGMENT STATEMENT AND USES

  Manager Morales-Stevens provided the report.

  Annette Kondo suggested that the statement be in the present tense. She said
  it’s a living pledge to acknowledge the indigenous community. She was upset
  with the recent pickleball discussions and didn’t want this statement to be an
  empty document.

  Jonathan Vivanti expressed disappointment over pickleball court discussions, he
  does not believe the city council knows the historical significance.

  The committee would like to include a list of uses for the statement, one of them
  being that the statement should be used as a reference when the city council
  makes decisions.

  At 5:34 p.m., there was a short break to confirm terms and spelling with the tribal
  leaders, the meeting resumed at 5:48 p.m.

  The committee decided not to rush to finalize a statement, they would like to
  take the time to find a consensus. They made some edits to the statement such
  as using the term “unceded villages”, instead of Sibagna.

  5. ADJOURNMENT

  MEMORANDUM
DATE:  January 17, 2024

TO:  LAS Advisory Committee

FROM:  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Manager

SUBJECT:  LAND ACKOWLEDGEMENT STATEMENT AND USES

BACKGROUND

At the September 14, 2021 LAS Advisory Committee Meeting, the Committee requested
that staff develop a Purpose Statement and a list of questions for the tribal leaders based
on the Committee’s discussion. At the October 6 meeting the purpose statement and
questions were approved with amendments. The approved statement is as follows: The
Land Acknowledgement Statement serves as a clear and ongoing commitment from the
City of San Gabriel to respect and acknowledge the native peoples of San Gabriel for their
past, current and future contributions to the region. At the May 9, 2022 meeting the
committee provided verbiage for the statement and directed staff to return to the next
meeting with a draft statement. At the September 13, 2023 meeting the committee
developed a revised statement and staff provided it to trial leaders for feedback.

PROPOSED LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT STATEMENT (LAS)

The City of San Gabriel resides on the lands of the unceded villages of the region’s first
peoples. The City acknowledges the ancestors of these villages, those collectivized at the
San Gabriel Mission as the Gabrieleño, and its responsibility to educate residents about
the enduring legacy of this vibrant community.

POSSIBLE USES FOR THE LAS STATEMENT

The Committee has expressed interest and a need for the City’s land acknowledgement
statement to make a larger impact than simply a statement. Below is what was developed
at the May 9 meeting.
  • Post on the City Website
  • Read aloud at City meetings and functions
  • Post at the front of the Mission Playhouse and/ or City Hall
   Land Acknowledgement Statement and Uses
  January 17, 2024
  Page 2

  •  Map of the indigenous villages with the statement

STAFF RECCOMENDATION

Staff recommend that the committee review and approve with or without amendments
the proposed land acknowledgement statement and proposed uses. Upon the
committee’s approval the staff will present the recommendations to the tribal leaders and
upon approval staff will present it to the Human Equity, Access, and Relations (HEAR) and
Historical Preservation and Cultural Resource Commissions for approval. If the two
commissions approve the statement it will be presented to City Council.
